changes.reason: The original level-one valid profile and invalid windowLog 99 are checked through concrete value validation. This does not install seven compression fields in a live context: ZSTD_CCtx_setCParams, its allocation/setup path, and bulk context mutation remain unported.

The original level-one valid profile and invalid windowLog 99 are checked through concrete value validation. This does not install seven compression fields in a live context: ZSTD_CCtx_setCParams, its allocation/setup path, and bulk context mutation remain unported.

The pinned minimum reference level is exposed and checked as -131072, including normalization below the minimum. This original group only queries the minimum; no operational numeric compression level is claimed.

The reference default-level getter assertion is preserved through DEFAULT_LEVEL == 3, default request construction, and level-zero normalization/query equivalence. The reference level is distinct from live named encoder policies.

The exact zero-initialized raw record with windowLog 10, hashLog 19 and chainLog 19 is adjusted for source 1000 and dictionary 100000; hashLog 18 and chainLog 17 are asserted. Rust uses typed known source size and validates the resulting concrete record.
The original default level-three, unknown-source, no-dictionary profile passes concrete seven-field validation. C public size zero is spelled SourceSize::Unknown in the Rust query.

Detached request getters preserve default level/hash auto, explicit hashLog 6 across a level-seven change, and restoration by Default. Supported live settings remain unchanged through partial headers, input, Flush, Finish and rejected configuration, and session/parameter resets are exercised separately. Numeric level/hash getters are not attached to live compression, and Rust retains its explicit Finished/reset protocol and checksum/pledge defaults.

Concrete records reject the original invalid strategy u32::MAX and preserve all seven valid level-derived fields, including level 12. Supported live option replacement rejects invalid windows atomically. There is no seven-field ZSTD_CCtx_setCParams bulk installer, so the original live all-fields getter and invalid-strategy bulk atomicity assertions remain unported.

Reference frame defaults preserve content-size=true, checksum=false and dictionary-ID=true. Supported live option replacement verifies false/true/false for the original {0,1,1} FParams flags, as well as emitted metadata and exact decoding. Rust live defaults enable checksum, and no separate C-style ZSTD_CCtx_setFParams/getParameter API is claimed.

The scalar subset validates all seven level-derived fields and rejects invalid strategy; the live subset verifies supported frame flags, getter preservation and invalid-window atomicity. Combined compression/frame bulk installation and invalid-strategy rollback across all original live numeric fields remain unported. Reference checksum-disabled defaults remain separate from Rust checksum-enabled defaults.

A shared raw dictionary can be selected before supported options are installed; a separate pinned formatted dictionary follows the same configuration path and its emitted frames are independently C-decoded. The original compression-profile-specific CDict, level-one/hashLog-12 controls and C attachment-parameter inheritance are not implemented.

Both dictionary/options installation orders produce identical complete frames and exact decoding for Greedy, Chain and Lazy. Original 10 KiB dictionary/100 KiB source dimensions are retained using declared RDG(0.5,0.0,seed 0) data and its first 10 KiB, not the inherited mutable C CNBuffer. Operational level seven and C-specific dictionary preparation remain unported.

Persistent dictionary selection and complete deterministic frame bytes survive session reset with the original 10 KiB/100 KiB dimensions and declared RDG(0.5,0.0,seed 0) corpus under each named policy. Rust reset clears the pledge, so the same supported options are explicitly restored; this does not claim the inherited C corpus, numeric default-level execution or automatic next-frame protocol.

Parameter-only reset clears dictionary handles while preserving Finished/counters; an explicit session reset then enables plain encoding. Full reset also clears unclaimed/claimed prefixes. With declared 10 KiB/100 KiB RDG data, useful dictionary frames differ in size from the cleared frames, which exactly match fresh Rust defaults and decode without a dictionary. Parameter/full resets restore Greedy/checksum-enabled/no-pledge defaults even after Chain/Lazy; C default-level execution and automatic next-frame semantics remain distinct.

Negative-level reference profiles can be inspected, but operational numeric compression levels are not implemented. The original level -1 simple-versus-advanced compression result-size comparison has not been ported; detached scalar queries do not establish this execution contract.

The original level-two, enabled long-distance matching and windowLog-18 order permutations require operational numeric levels and LDM. Their equal compressed size and XXH64 assertions remain unported; detached override-order queries and named-policy dictionary/options ordering do not establish these output semantics.

The original level-two, enabled long-distance matching and windowLog-18 order permutations require operational numeric levels and LDM. Their equal compressed size and XXH64 assertions remain unported; detached override-order queries and named-policy dictionary/options ordering do not establish these output semantics.

Decoder options and reusable session reset exist, but this original loop over numeric decoder parameter bounds/getters/setters and reset-to-default values is not implemented. The new parameter/full resets are encoder-only and do not reset a decoder caller's output/window resource policy.

All three original fieldwise level-one dictionary-query equalities are preserved for source sizes 16 KiB-1 and 128 KiB-1 and dictionary sizes 400, 10000 and 100000. Value equality replaces C memcmp, and public C source zero maps explicitly to SourceSize::Unknown.

The original level-one unknown-source profile is unchanged after adjustment with a 400-byte dictionary, while known source 500 plus dictionary 400 resolves windowLog 10. All fields are compared without C struct-padding assumptions; public C source zero maps explicitly to Unknown.

Configured supported options remain visible through streaming progress and explicit session reset, with exact frame reuse/decode checks. Numeric ZSTD_initCStream_srcSize(level 11), live compression-level getters and C automatic next-frame behavior are not implemented; Rust reset also clears its per-frame pledge.

Concrete reference profiles retain all seven fields, while supported live settings survive processing/session reset and restore documented Rust defaults on parameter/full reset. This does not port level-nine ZSTD_initCStream_advanced bulk initialization or its live numeric badParameters comparison; reference profiles are inspection-only.

A detached typed request accepts an INT_MAX source hint and reports it unchanged, rejects values above INT_MAX atomically and treats zero as automatic. The original negative -1 C argument is unrepresentable at the u32 Rust setter. A small positive hint changes unknown-size resolution and leaves known sizes unchanged, but hints are not operational live encoder controls.

A bounded adapter for the enclosing new-API randomized driver repeats 128 supported-option schedules with byte-identical encoding and fragmented exact decoding. Separate source-anchored live tests preserve configured getters through partial output, Flush/Finish and rejected changes, including selected dictionary/prefix/reset cases. The full original randomized dictionary schedule, opaque parameter bulk API, numeric level/strategy execution, LDM, worker/job-boundary updates and rsyncable matrix remain unported; these deterministic named-policy adapters do not reproduce that full driver.
